clue.text: Provokes previous lover with quotes

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: Someone is stirred up by a former partner throwing their own words back at them.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone is to stir or provoke a reaction in them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Less challenging time for one's religious festival

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in

parts.note: easier means less difficult
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A religious holiday offers someone an easier stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring Christian feast marks the resurrection of Jesus.

clue.text: Pressure middle distance runner before race to ignore article

indicators.note: before puts the runner ahead of what follows

parts.note: Sebastian Coe was a British Olympic champion at 1500 metres

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A miler is under pressure before a race, told to disregard a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a newspaper story but is the grammatical article A, dropped from RACE to leave RCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressure someone is to force or push them into acting, which is to compel.

clue.text: Intimidated doctor treated hen

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet's treatment frightened the chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intimidated has been menaced or frightened by threats.

clue.text: Shilling — money for perfume

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence
a cent is a small unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone pays a shilling for a bottle of fragrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume is a pleasant smell, and also the liquid that gives one.

clue.text: Lectured son about former education

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
old means former, as in an old flame

explanation.surface: A parent gives their son a talking-to about what schooling used to be like.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lectured means being told off at length, so it matches a telling-off or reprimand.

clue.text: Insect — it's prepared for entomologist?

indicators.note: prepared means made up or worked into shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect specimen has been mounted for the bug expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an entomologist is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entomologist studies insects, so is one kind of researcher in the natural sciences.

clue.text: Road signs regularly going missing? God!

indicators.note: every other letter drops out, leaving the even-placed letters of road signs

explanation.surface: An exasperated driver curses missing road signs.
explanation.definitionFit: This chief Norse deity ruled Asgard, so is a god of mythology.

clue.text: Stirring little drink — a sign of nerves

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, usually whisky
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A nervous person takes a small whisky to steady themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring means exciting or moving, like a thrilling, theatrical moment.

clue.text: Daughter impressing naughty child's removed bandage

indicators.note: removed says these letters are taken away

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A daughter tries to impress by taking off a naughty child's bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a covering placed on a wound, like a bandage.

clue.text: Guide animal

definitions.meaning: to guide something is to direct its course, as with a wheel
a young castrated bullock raised for beef

explanation.surface: A guide dog or similar working beast.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is directing a vehicle's course; the other is a bullock reared for beef.

clue.text: Take out rubbish late and I'm in trouble, finally

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for putting the bins out late and admits they are in hot water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out rubbish' looks like the chore of the definition, but 'rubbish' is the anagram signal on LATE and I'M IN, giving ELIMINAT; 'finally' adds the E ending trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out a rival or target is to get rid of them, the sense of removing completely.

clue.text: Captivating English knight by singing

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
chanting is a form of singing in unison or on one note

explanation.surface: A singing English knight charms his audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Something captivating holds you spellbound, which is the bewitching sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Flipping go mad

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the word for go is read backwards

parts.note: to have a go is to have a stab at something

explanation.surface: Someone flipping out and going crazy, in slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like the slang for mad, so 'go mad' reads as one phrase; in fact 'Flipping' signals the turnaround and 'mad' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal slang for crazy, like batty or having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Expected winners succeeded after following a very old upper-class ritual

indicators.note: after says the preceding piece goes at the end

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
U denotes upper-class usage, as in U and non-U
a rite is a ritual ceremony
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: The bookies' picks win after following some ancient posh ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Favourites are the competitors most fancied to win, with the shortest odds.

clue.text: Result of exercises in airports, possibly?

definitions.text: Result of exercises in airports, possibly?

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hurrying through airport terminals leaves travellers sweating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles IN and AIRPORTS into RSPIRATION; read as a whole, the clue also describes sweat, which is what exercise produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweat is the familiar outcome of physical exertion, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Expelled South American writer departs with editor

parts.note: US means American
a pen is something you write with
D is the abbreviation for departs, as in timetables

explanation.surface: A South American author is thrown out, leaving with their editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspended pupil has been excluded from school for a time, a temporary expulsion.

clue.text: Got a cold and left almost embarrassed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to quit a place is to leave it
red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone caught a cold and went off feeling sheepish.
explanation.definitionFit: To have acquired something is to have obtained it, a synonym of got.

clue.text: Silly NASA unfortunately losing large probe

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters are jumbled
losing means one letter is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: The space agency foolishly loses a big space probe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probe' looks like a spacecraft in this surface, but it is the definition in its sense of an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a close examination or investigation, which is what a probe is.

clue.text: Rabbit turning around a tree initially

indicators.note: around says the word for turning wraps round the next letters

parts.note: a conversion is a turning, as in turning to a new faith or use

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of tree

explanation.surface: A rabbit circles a tree at the start of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal, but it is British rhyming slang: 'rabbit and pork' means talk, so to rabbit on is to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a rabbit is a chat or talk, from the rhyme rabbit and pork.

clue.text: Police leader formerly protecting queen's procession

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the singer surrounds the next letter

parts.note: Sting was the frontman of the band The Police
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A former police chief guards the queen's parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like the force, but it is the rock band The Police, whose leader was Sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of people or things is a line of them one after another, like a procession.

clue.text: A virile chap turned up embracing 50 grown-ups

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes round the other
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a stud is a sexually virile man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A macho man arrives with fifty adults in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses STUD to DUTS, which then goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups are people who have reached maturity, the informal word for them.

clue.text: Some bug likes fruit

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An insect has a taste for a certain fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Jamaican citrus, a cross between grapefruit and tangerine, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Famous church with red table vandalised

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-known church suffers when someone wrecks its red table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous church' reads as one phrase, but 'Famous' alone is the definition; 'vandalised' signals the rearrangement of the red table.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means widely renowned and praised, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Finished? Fixed with minutes to go

indicators.note: to go means that letter must leave

parts.note: mended means repaired or fixed

explanation.surface: A repairer asks if the job is done, with minutes left on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ended is over or concluded, which is finished.

clue.text: Go round hill outside university

indicators.note: outside means the hill sits around the other letter

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone walks round a hill outside a university town.
explanation.definitionFit: To tour a place is to travel around it, visiting its sights.

clue.text: Grass around small pool came back

indicators.note: around says the grass wraps round the following letters

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pond is a small pool of still water

explanation.surface: Reeds grow around a little pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to answer or reply, which is coming back to someone.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a court hearing in which a case is judged
a ... run, an experiment to try something out

explanation.surface: An audiometry check of someone's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case is heard before a judge, and an experiment tries something out: both senses of the word.

clue.text: Wanted gentleman without legal document? On the contrary

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the document goes round the gentleman rather than the reverse

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document, such as for property
sir is a respectful address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman is in demand despite lacking legal paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, and 'On the contrary' says the roles are the other way round: the document is the one outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired means longed for or wished for, the same as wanted.

clue.text: Democrat quits, dismissing Republican's plans

indicators.note: dismissing says one letter is thrown out and the other takes its place

parts.note: to resign is to quit a job
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Democrat steps down after a Republican's schemes are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: D takes the place of R in the word for quits.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs are plans or schemes, as when someone has designs on a job.
